privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page says what Translatv, the translated video call app at this address, does with information about you. Every statement here describes what the app's code does. The app is run by [OWNER: operator name], in [OWNER: jurisdiction]. Effective date: [OWNER: effective date].
privacy.age.p: You need an account to start or join a call. You must be at least [OWNER: minimum age] years old to have one.
privacy.stores.email: Your email address, in lowercase. It is how you sign in. The app sends no email to it.
privacy.stores.password: Your password, as a scrypt hash only. The password itself is never stored.
privacy.stores.name: The display name you choose, which the people you call see, and when you created the account.
privacy.stores.sessions: Your sign ins: each is a long random token, stored only as a hash, that lasts up to 30 days and is replaced every time it is used.
privacy.stores.dialect: The language and region you last chose, so the app can start in it.
privacy.stores.glossary: Your saved glossary: the short corrections you made to translations during your calls ({words} words or fewer, checked by fixed rules, saved when the call ends), up to {max} terms. It is private: it is used only to translate what you read, and is never shown to anyone else. You can see and delete every entry on your account page.
privacy.stores.calls: Your call history: for each call, a one way hash of the room code (never the code itself), who was on the other end, and when the call started and ended. The list of people you have called is worked out from this history and not stored on its own.
privacy.stores.blocks: The people you have blocked, and when.
privacy.stores.reports: Reports you make about someone: the reason you picked, any details you wrote (up to {detailsMax} characters), when, and who the report is about. Reports other people make about you are stored the same way.
privacy.never.p1: Audio and video never reach the server at all.
privacy.never.p2: Nothing anyone says or types in a call is stored. Transcripts, chat messages and the glossary shared in a room are held in the server's memory only while the call lasts, so that a browser which reconnects can catch up, and are gone when the room ends or the server restarts. The one exception is your own short corrections, described above. Nobody can download a transcript, and nothing from a call is attached to a report.
privacy.call.media: Audio and video go directly between the two browsers (peer to peer) and are encrypted between them. When a direct connection is not possible and this server has a relay (TURN) set up, the encrypted media passes through that relay, which cannot decrypt it.
privacy.call.stun: To find a direct route, each browser asks a public STUN server for its own internet address. Unless the operator changes it, that is Google's (stun.l.google.com), which therefore sees your IP address.
privacy.call.relay: The server relays the messages that set up the connection, and the text of the call: each person's finished sentences and typed chat messages.
privacy.call.speech: Speech recognition is done by your own browser, and only on your own microphone. Depending on the browser, it may send your audio to the browser's maker (for example Google, for Chrome) to transcribe it. Where on device recognition is available, you can switch to it and your audio then stays on your device. The call screen shows which one is in use.
privacy.translate.p: When someone finishes a sentence or sends a chat message and the other person reads a different language, the server sends that text to Anthropic's API to translate it. With it go a few recent lines of the conversation for context, the names used in that call, the languages and regions, and the glossary terms that apply, including the reader's own saved terms. Nothing is sent when both people speak the same language, or when the reader has turned translation off. [OWNER: the Anthropic terms and data retention that apply to this deployment.]
privacy.logs.p1: The server's logs record events with counts, durations and opaque identifiers: a random account id (never an email address) and a hash of the room code. They never contain what was said or typed, names, email addresses, passwords, tokens or the details of a report. When a connection is cut off for sending too much too fast, its IP address is logged. Logs are kept for [OWNER: log retention period].
privacy.logs.p2: To enforce those limits the server also keeps IP addresses in memory, never on disk. Failed sign ins are counted against a keyed hash of the email address for 15 minutes, to stop password guessing.
privacy.logs.p3: Each translation request adds a line to a spending ledger: the time, the model, the number of tokens, the cost, the hash of the room code, which server made it, whether the person who runs this app was on the call, and a tag for whoever spoke the line. The tag is made with a key only the server holds, so the ledger cannot be matched to an account without it. It holds no account id, name, email address, or anything said.
privacy.browser.p: Your browser keeps your sign in, your chosen theme, language and speech engine, and a short lived token that lets a reloaded tab get its seat back in a call. They stay on your device. There are no advertising or analytics cookies, and the page loads nothing from other sites.
privacy.delete.p1: You can delete your account from your account page, after typing your password again. That deletes the account and everything it holds: your email address, password hash, name, sign ins, language choice, saved glossary, call history, the people you blocked, and any block someone else made of you. Deleted data is overwritten in the database file, not just marked as free space.
privacy.delete.p2: Some things are kept, because they are part of someone else's record. The other person's history of a call with you stays, without your name on it. Invites you made or used stay, without your account on them. Reports you made, and reports other people made about you, stay without your account attached, so the person who runs this app can still act on them; they are kept for [OWNER: report retention period]. The spending ledger is not changed, and holds nothing about you.
privacy.share.p: Only those this page names: the other person in your call, Anthropic for translation, your browser's speech service if it uses one, the STUN server and any relay, and the company that hosts this server, [OWNER: hosting provider].
privacy.rights.p: [OWNER: the rights people have under the law that applies (access, correction, deletion, objection, complaint to a regulator), and how to use them.]

support.title: Help and support
support.help.with: Write to support, saying what happened and which browser and device you were using. Never send your password.
support.help.without: This server has no support address set up. Ask the person who invited you.
support.safety.call: During a call: open Settings, then choose Report or block.
support.safety.history: After a call: on your account page, open Recent calls and choose Report or block beside the call.
support.safety.block: Blocking someone means the two of you are never put in a call together again, and it ends a call you are in with them. They are not told. You can unblock them under Blocked people on your account page.
support.safety.report: A report goes to the person who runs this app. Pick what happened, and add details if you like. Nothing from the call is attached, because calls are not recorded.
support.safety.danger: If someone is in danger, contact your local emergency services first.
support.delete.p: On your account page, choose Delete account and type your password again. It cannot be undone. The privacy policy says exactly what is deleted and what is kept.
support.media.h: The microphone or camera does not work
support.media.allow: Allow the microphone (and the camera, for video) when the browser asks. If you said no, allow it in the browser's settings for this site, then reload the page.
support.media.busy: Close any other app that is using the microphone or camera.
support.media.secure: The page has to be opened over https, or from localhost. A plain http address cannot use the microphone or camera.
support.stt.browser: Live subtitles need a browser with speech recognition, such as Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox has none: the call and text chat work there, but subtitles do not.
support.stt.ios: On iPhone and iPad, speech recognition is a separate permission from the microphone: Settings, then Privacy and Security, then Speech Recognition. Then reload the page.
support.stt.drops: If subtitles keep dropping, reload the page, or carry on with text chat.
support.net.h: The call does not connect, or the video freezes
support.net.firewall: Some networks, such as strict office or school ones, block direct connections between browsers. Subtitles and chat still work through the server when video cannot get through. Another network often helps.
support.net.grace: If your connection drops, the app keeps your seat for a minute. Reloading the page within that minute puts you back in the same call.
support.net.restart: A server restart ends every call. Start a new one.
